10.1002_adfm.75028: High polarity of Mg 2+ results in unsatisfied interactions with the cathode host lattice, giving rise to sluggish Mg 2+ diffusion and thus surface “self‐passivation” caused by irreversible insertion/extraction of Mg 2+ , impeding development of magnesium metal batteries (MMBs). Herein, we pioneer a Defect Chemistry‐Inspired synergistic strategy of synchronously Spin‐State Modulation and Adaptive Microstructural Reformation, thereby resolving the inherent thermodynamic–kinetic conflict to improve Mg 2+ storage. Combining first‐principles calculations with advanced characterization, the intrinsic inertness of the V‐3d 0 orbital in Cu 3 VS 4 was activated by filling electrons to induce a spin state change after introducing Na + , which enhanced the electron hopping process for rapid charge compensation to unlock Mg 2+ storage ability. Furthermore, the cathode undergoes a self‐driven structural evolution into a microcrystalline/amorphous hybrid, improved the cathode‐electrolyte interface and Internal reaction site to balance subsequent Mg 2+ adsorption and mobility. The optimized material, C@A‐N‐0.5, delivers a high specific capacity of 140 mAh g −1 at 40 mA g −1 (92% of capacity over rarely reported 300 cycles), and it had over 100 mAh g −1 at 200 mA g −1 for 1000 cycles, far outperforming the unmodified Cu 3 VS 4 with negligible Mg 2+ storage. This work provides mechanistic insights and materials design pathways for high‐performance MMBs cathodes based on transition metal sulfides.
10.1021_acs.langmuir.6c04679: Developing low-cost and durable non-noble-metal electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential for efficient alkaline water electrolysis. Herein, FeCoNiCu medium-entropy alloy electrodes with tunable dendritic architectures were prepared on Cu substrates by one-step potentiostatic electrodeposition in a choline chloride–urea (ChCl–urea) deep eutectic solvent (DES). The effects of deposition potential, deposition time, and CuCl concentration on the alloy composition, morphology, and OER performance were systematically investigated. Under the optimized conditions of −1.4 V vs Ag, 2 h, and 0.2 M CuCl, a short and thick three-dimensional dendritic network was obtained. This structure provided abundant accessible catalytic sites and efficient electron-transport pathways. The optimized FeCoNiCu electrode required an overpotential of 285 mV (corresponding to 1.515 V vs RHE) to reach 10 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH, which was 107 mV lower than that of a commercial RuO2–IrO2 catalyst under the same evaluation conditions. The electrode also showed favorable charge-transfer kinetics, with an Rct of 2.183 Ω cm2, and maintained stable activity during a 120 h chronopotentiometric test and 2000 CV cycles. Post-OER XPS analysis suggests that Fe, Co, and Ni were reconstructed into oxide/oxyhydroxide-rich catalytically relevant oxyhydroxide-rich species, whereas Cu was less extensively oxidized and may contribute mainly to electrical conductivity and structural stabilization. This work provides a DES-assisted electrodeposition strategy for designing macroscopically homogeneous dendritic medium-entropy alloy electrocatalysts for alkaline OER.
10.1039_d6ta03045a: The synergistic effects between N-doped carbon and Fe 3 C/Fe enable Fe 3 C/Fe@NC to overcome NRR's trilemma, delivering a high NH 3 yield, remarkable faradaic efficiency, and good stability, thereby providing a viable heterostructure strategy for NRR.
